By Dan Primack · Nov 25, 2026

🦃 Pass the gravy: As we head into the Thanksgiving holiday, a note of gratitude to you for subscribing, reading, and responding to these morning missives. You are the best part of this amazing job, and it's a privilege to be in your inbox. We'll chat again on Monday...

📺 NEW: Maryland Gov. Wes Moore joins "The Axios Show" to discuss Nvidia and Jensen Huang, AI regulation, and his 2028 plans. Watch the episode ... Subscribe to our YouTube.

Top of the Morning
 

Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios
 

Emptying out the notebook before meal prep...

😱 Look out below: Anthropic's IPO pop has turned into a thud, leaving retail investors holding the bag.

  • Shares closed yesterday at $81.90 — below the $83 IPO price and 26.5% below the first post-IPO trades. They opened this morning down another 5% at $77.93 per share.
  • Same story at SpaceX, where shares today opened below their IPO price, 25% below the first post-IPO trades, and around 44% below the first-day high.
  • Yes, these are just moments in time and shouldn't worry long-term investors in either company. But they could be causing some sleepless nights over at OpenAI, assuming it still plans to go public in early 2027. Big fund managers might push much harder on price than they did with either Anthropic or SpaceX, and a lot of retail investors might sit it out entirely — not wanting more wounds to lick.

⛳ Next shot: BC Partners Credit this morning announced that it's acquired a majority stake in GSE Worldwide, a sports management agency known for representing pro golfers like Bryson DeChambeau.

  • BC already held a minority stake, but bought the rest from Gatemore Capital Management.
  • This comes on the heels of BC bailing on its plans for LIV 2.0, and reports that it was working on a DIP plan that could have created yet another version. But a source assures me that "LIV 3.0 is dead" and that GSE is a standalone investment.

🏛️ What to watch: Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Md.), incoming chair of the House Judiciary Committee, says that he plans to pursue his investigation of 1789 Capital — the growth equity firm that Donald Trump Jr. joined just days after his father's election victory in 2024.

  • It's something I discussed with Trump Jr. and 1789 founder Omeed Malik last week at Axios BFD, given that the firm had previously declined certain information requests from Raskin.
  • But Raskin might want a private equity primer before holding hearings. On CNN last night, he said the firm was "worth" $3 billion when he meant its AUM. He also said "their stock has shot up," even though 1789 doesn't have a public stock.

📸 Speaking of Axios BFD: Some of you emailed to ask what happened to our planned interview with Flock CEO Garrett Langley.

  • In short, Langley reached out in late October to say a personal conflict had arisen and he could no longer attend. At the same time, however, Langley turned down a different Axios request at a different date and said at a private event that he'd prefer to never do media interviews again. So who really knows.
  • It's a shame, because Flock has raised over $1 billion and really does have a compelling story to tell. Keeping quiet is unlikely to make the storm dissipate.

💰 Corporate venturing: Payward, owner of crypto exchange Kraken, earlier this week announced that it had acquired Tribe Capital.

  • Tribe was co-founded by Payward co-CEO Arjun Sethi, years before he joined Payward, and has raised over $2 billion for various VC funds.
  • Sethi tells me that the firm will continue to raise money from outside LPs, but now will have "better access" to equity and debt products for its portfolio. Plus expanded distribution.
  • Don't be surprised to see Payward buy other managers, while also augmenting the Tribe team.

Also: Sethi didn't respond to my questions on Foundation, a Tribe portfolio company that stopped paying its employees last month. This is the one led by Sankaet Pathak, who founded Foundation while customers of his prior company (Synapse) were still unable to access around $50 million in deposits.

  • Oh, Pathak also borrowed $4.6 million from Foundation last year to buy a luxury home.
  • At the time of the Tribe investment, we wrote: "Silicon Valley has a history of giving founders a second chance, but usually it waits until the initial fire has been extinguished."
 
 
The BFD
 

Illustration: Natalie Peeples/Axios
 

Airbus (Paris: AIR) agreed to sell its U.S. space business to Cerberus Capital Management.

Why it's the BFD: Airbus caught some congressional heat for allegedly providing satellite imagery of U.S. military assets to China, just ahead of the Iran war.

  • Now the business not only moves into U.S. hands, but the firm was founded and previously led by Steve Feinberg — who currently serves as the Pentagon's No. 2 official behind Pete Hegseth.

Zoom in: The business manufactures satellites near Florida's Kennedy Space Center for both national security and commercial customers.

  • Expect the deal to close by year-end.

The bottom line: "Airbus is in the process of merging its satellite operations business with Leonardo and Thales to create a European joint venture that would compete with Elon Musk's SpaceX." — Leen Al-Rashdan, Bloomberg
 
 
Venture Capital Deals
 

• Stripe is in talks for a new employee tender that could value the payments giant at around $200b, per the WSJ. axios.link/4eYYIlb

• Eon, an Israeli cloud backup company, is in talks for new funding at a $6b valuation, per Globes. axios.link/4l9eNbN

⚡ Peak Energy, a Denver-based sodium-ion battery maker, raised $49m in Series B extension funding. GM Ventures led the equity tranche, while HSBC provided debt. axios.link/4l8lPxw

• Avicena, a Sunnyvale, Calif.-based optical interconnect platform, raised $100m in Series C funding. InterVest led, joined by Tiger Global, Cerberus Capital Management, SK hynix Ventures, Samsung Catalyst Fund, AMD Ventures, Prosperity7 Ventures, Diamond Edge Ventures, and Hitachi Ventures. axios.link/4kzwQb2

⚡️ HoloSolis, a French solar manufacturer, raised €15m in Series A funding from Crédit Agricole Group, Algebris, Trina Solar, StarCharge, and insiders Calès Technologies, Forming, and Ecolab. axios.link/4j7lQ23

• Dante Security, an agentic security startup, raised $10m in seed funding. NFX led, joined by Alpha Drive and Inovia. axios.link/4eW42WF

⚡️ Mechademy, a Houston-based provider of software to model and monitor natural gas turbines, raised $9.5m in Series A funding, per Axios Pro. Silverton Partners led, joined by CSL Ventures. axios.link/4jeJzh5

• Bayesline, an NYC-based analytics engine for hedge funds and asset managers, raised $4m. Nyca Partners led, joined by insiders YC and 468 Capital. axios.link/3VfcOYS

• Whereable.ai, a South Korean developer of autonomous driving tech, raised $2.3m in pre-Series A funding from Quad Ventures, Lotte Ventures, and Korea Credit Guarantee Fund. axios.link/3X6JJ2w

• Sequent, a London-based startup using AI to find software bugs, raised $2.2m in pre-seed funding led by Frachtis and Metaplanet. axios.link/4jCsnDi

🐟 Aqura Systems, a Scottish robotic monitoring platform for fish farms, raised £2.1m led by Archangels alongside Scottish Enterprise. axios.link/3WQo4f1

⚡️ Good Heat, a Dutch developer of zero-emissions industrial heat, raised €2m. SET Ventures led, joined by Shell Ventures and Investible. axios.link/4zCOq1t

• Accent Equity agreed to acquire Plantasjen, a Norwegian garden products retailer, from Ratos for around $40m. axios.link/3VGWssp

• Advent International is weighing a bid for French testing firm Bureau Veritas (Paris: BVI), whose major shareholders include Wendel, per Bloomberg. axios.link/3XoRaCf

• DRT Aerospace, a GenNx360 Capital Partners portfolio company, acquired Duke Manufacturing, a Willoughby, Ohio-based maker of aerospace engine components. axios.link/4ASboCY

• FPE invested in SEP2, a U.K. cybersecurity and managed security service provider. axios.link/4kAJBCe

⚡️ Reinova Partners bought the U.K. district heating business of Swedish utility Vattenfall. axios.link/4kBJyGb
 
 
Liquidity Events
 

• Atairos is seeking to sell Ocean Outdoor, a U.K. outdoor advertising operator that could fetch around £800m, per Reuters. axios.link/4j9Gccx

• Parker-Hannifin (NYSE: PH) completed its $2.55b acquisition of Circor Aerospace, a Corona, Calif.-based maker of flow control and motion control products, from KKR. axios.link/4l2RjVO
 
 
More M&A
 

🐟 Bolton Group of Italy bought Italian seafood processor Foodlab. axios.link/4kAx0Pk

• BYD, China's largest automaker, is in talks to buy Ineos Automotive's manufacturing plant in Hambach, France. axios.link/4A2M7G3

• CF Industries (NYSE: CF) agreed to buy the Faustina ammonia plant in Louisiana from The Mosaic Co. (NYSE: MOS) for around $600m. axios.link/4A0gahC

• Al Gore agreed to buy the Carthage Courier newspaper in Tennessee. axios.link/3WV2hTq

☕ Starbucks (Nasdaq: SBUX) picked banks for the sale of its Japan business, per Bloomberg. axios.link/4tjqnDa
 
 
Fundraising
 

• FirstLook Partners, an LA-based fund-of-funds and direct venture firm, is raising $75m for its second fund, per an SEC filing.
 
 
It's Personnel
 

• Sidley is hiring 25 lawyers in its London office, including private equity partners Marco Compagnoni and Jonathan Wood, from Weil, Gotshal & Manges. It previously added more than 35 Weil lawyers to its NYC and SF offices. axios.link/4kw0uhn
 
 
Final Numbers
 
Data: Bureau of Economic Analysis; Chart: Courtenay Brown/Axios

The U.S. economy grew substantially faster this summer than initially thought, per new data released this morning.

  • GDP expanded at a 4.3% annualized rate, up from the 3.4% initially reported and nearly twice the rate of 2.2% in the second quarter.

Other new economic data: Personal income jumped 0.7% in October while inflation-adjusted consumer spending stalled, pushing the saving rate up to 4.1% from 3.6% the prior month.

  • The PCE price index— the Fed's preferred inflation gauge — rose 3.8% from a year earlier, up from 3.6% in September. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, accelerated to 3.3% from 3.1%.
